Why Slow Reading Wins

Reading slowly is a skill that most people lose after school. The argument here is simple: attention is a finite resource, and long-form text rewards spending it deliberately. This paragraph exists to give the extractor enough body text to treat this element as the main content of the page, which is what readability looks for when scoring candidates.

A second paragraph continues the argument with more sentences so that the text density stays high. E-ink devices make this easier because they remove the notification stream that competes for the same attention budget on a phone or laptop.

Finally, a closing thought: the goal is not to read less, but to read with intent. Related post.
